page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ae.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9T34 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. It includes 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, and it lacks dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a strong single-core capability, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core results falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is average at 47.71 GB/sec for read-only and 27.73 GB/sec for write operations, while small-block cached read bandwidth is weak. Cryptographic and vector instruction sets are supported, including AVX-512 and AES, though Passmark CPU extended instructions and encryption tests register in the bottom 25%.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.g8ae.large is its limited multi-core scaling and poor database and web serving throughput, with Passmark database operations and static web serving benchmarks ranking in the bottom 10%. Given these constraints, the instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that rely heavily on single-threaded CPU performance rather than parallel processing or high-throughput database transactions. It is best suited for lightweight general-purpose applications, single-threaded background tasks, basic text processing, and development environments that do not require local NVMe storage or high multi-core density.
